valāhaka.p: [Vāri+vāhaka] (pu) CL=7 [Vāriṃ vahatīti valāhako. Vāri-changes va-.  Va of Vāhaka changes La-. Dhāna,ṭī.47-8.moga,1.47.nīti,sutta.1340.valāhaka-saṃ. Balāhaga-prā.]  The rain. The rain cloud. Valāhaka(pu) [vālenta+ahi+ṇvu. Valāha(1)+ka.] The rain Deva is named Valāhaka. See - Valāhakakāyika. There are five Devas- (1) Sītavalāhaka= A Deva who causes coldness. (2) Uṇuvalāhaka= A Deva who causes to be hot. (3) Abbhavalāhaka= A Deva who causes the rain cloud. (4) Ātavalāhaka= A Deva who causes the wind. (5) Vassavalāhaka= A Deva who causes falling rain. Valāhaka(pu,na) [valāhaka+ṇa] (Pu) (1) (A leader horse or the horse King) is named Valāhaka. (2) (The lower garment of a man) that color is like the rain cloud. (Na) (1) Raining water. (The water that is falling down from the rain cloud). (4) The pearl is called Valāhaka. (4) The pearl that comes from the rain cloud.
pn: Valāhaka 01. A family of horses from which the Assaratana of a Cakkavatti is supplied (Khp-a. 172; MN.iii.174). He is best among animals, because he takes his rider away from all danger (MN-a.ii.616). Noble chargers come from the Valāhaka stock. Dhp-a.iii.248.
Valāhaka 02. The name of the horse of Mahā Sudassana. He is all white, with a crow-black head and a dark mane. DN.ii.174; cp. SN.iii.145.
